o: Blocks acetylcholine release, chemically reducing sphincter tone
Increases nitric oxide in the sphincter
questions.e: Botulinum toxin blocks acetylcholine release, chemically reducing sphincter tone; lateral internal sphincterotomy does the same surgically.

steps.x: It asks for the mechanism: link the finding in the stem to the underlying process.

clues: botulinum toxin injected into the internal anal sphincter
steps.x: A toxin injected into the sphincter after medical treatment failed.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Blocks acetylcholine release, chemically reducing sphincter tone.

elim: That is lateral internal sphincterotomy.
That is GTN.
Not its action.
That is a laxative.

steps.x: **A. Blocks acetylcholine release, chemically reducing sphincter tone.** Botulinum = chemical sphincter relaxation; sphincterotomy = surgical.

questions.stem: A medical student sees two patients with anal fissures. One has a posterior midline fissure after constipation. The other has a fissure at the 9 o'clock position and is under investigation for Crohn's disease. The student asks why the second site is more concerning.
questions.q: Which is the best explanation?
o: It suggests underlying disease rather than simple trauma from a hard stool
Lateral fissures always heal on their own
Lateral fissures are caused by hard stools
Off-midline fissures only occur in children
The lateral anoderm has no nerve supply
questions.e: Simple fissures come from hard-stool trauma at the poorly perfused posterior midline; Crohn's, malignancy and STI do not follow that distribution, so an off-midline fissure suggests underlying disease.

steps.x: It asks for the mechanism: link the finding in the stem to the underlying process.
Typical midline trauma versus an off-midline lesion with possible Crohn's.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: It suggests underlying disease rather than simple trauma from a hard stool.

elim: Not true, and not why it is concerning.
Hard stools typically cause posterior midline fissures.
They occur at any age.
Lateral fissures are also painful.

steps.x: **A. It suggests underlying disease rather than simple trauma from a hard stool.** Off-midline = think Crohn's, cancer or STI, not simple trauma.

questions.stem: A 31 year old man has a fissure in the posterior midline after passing a hard stool. His BP is 122/78 mmHg and pulse rate 68 bpm. His surgeon explains that most fissures occur at this site and are slow to heal there.
questions.q: Which is the most likely reason the posterior midline is affected?
o: Poor blood supply in a watershed area
questions.e: The posterior midline is a watershed area with poor blood supply, and with raised internal sphincter tone it heals poorly.

steps.x: It asks for the mechanism: link the finding in the stem to the underlying process.
Typical site, slow healing: think blood supply.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Poor blood supply in a watershed area.

elim: Gland infection causes abscesses and fistulae.
The external sphincter surrounds the canal.
Not the reason for fissures.
The anoderm is very sensitive, which is why fissures hurt.

steps.x: **D. Poor blood supply in a watershed area.** Posterior midline = watershed area with poor blood supply.
